sn22.47:1.2: “Bhikkhus, those ascetics and brahmins who regard anything as self in various ways all regard as self the five aggregates subject to clinging, or a certain one among them.
sn22.47:1.4: “Here, bhikkhus, the uninstructed worldling, who is not a seer of the noble ones and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma, who is not a seer of superior persons and is unskilled and undisciplined in their Dhamma,
sn22.47:1.5: regards form as self, or self as possessing form, or form as in self, or self as in form.
sn22.47:1.9: consciousness as self, or self as possessing consciousness, or consciousness as in self, or self as in consciousness.
sn22.47:2.1: “Thus this way of regarding things and the notion ‘I am’ have not vanished in him.
sn22.47:2.2: As ‘I am’ has not vanished, there takes place a descent of the five faculties—
sn22.47:2.3: of the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty.
sn22.47:2.4: There is, bhikkhus, the mind, there are mental phenomena, there is the element of ignorance.
sn22.47:2.5: When the uninstructed worldling is contacted by a feeling born of ignorance-contact, ‘I am’ occurs to him;
sn22.47:2.13: ‘I will be neither percipient nor nonpercipient’—these occur to him.
sn22.47:3.1: “The five faculties remain right there, bhikkhus,
sn22.47:3.2: but in regard to them the instructed noble disciple abandons ignorance and arouses true knowledge.
sn22.47:3.3: With the fading away of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge, ‘I am’ does not occur to him;
sn22.47:3.4: ‘I am this’ does not occur to him;
sn22.47:3.11: ‘I will be neither percipient nor nonpercipient’—these do not occur to him.”
